content:
- Overestimate prices after strong positive sentiment spikes; model tends to overshoot early in the forecast horizon.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is weak or negative; model fails to account for downward pressure.
- Forecast tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days; adjust for recent sentiment shifts to reduce lag.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to short-term volatility; smooth out sharp swings in forecast if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.
- When sentiment is consistently positive over 3+ days, model overweights upward momentum; reduce forecast slope after 3 consecutive positive sentiment days.
- If sentiment turns negative within 3 days, model fails to correct downward trend; apply downward bias of 1–2% per day of negative sentiment.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to overconfidence in early days; reduce forecast magnitude by 0.5–1.0% per day for days 1–7 if sentiment is weak.
